To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wall-mounted cylinders used in this investigation do indeed affect the flow structure and statistics of a turbulent boundary layer; that this effect is dependent on cylinder spacing, but is independent of the cylinder diameter; and that the effect of the cylinders is to increase the turbulent intensity and Reynolds stress in the region immediately downstream of the cylinders, but to decrease the turbulent intensity and the Reynolds stress in regions further downstream, where these quantities are reduced to levels lower than those of the undisturbed boundary layer.

the flow downstream of single-spanwise arrays of cylinders with H= 0.13 is dominated by tip vortex structures that are shed from the cylinders in a quasi-periodic fashion and are organized in a streamwise array.

the presence of wallmounted cylinders with AR = 1:5, H = 150, and a blockage ratio of less than 1% in a turbulent boundarylayer with Re = 1200 significantly modifies the velocity statistics and the coherent vortices in the logarithmic andouter regions of the boundary layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of wall-mounted cylinder arrays on turbulent boundary layers with Re 120000 and H= 0.13.
the effects of simple wall-mounted cylindrical obstacles on a turbulent boundary-layer flow.
the effects of wall-mounted cylinders with a low blockage ratio, small aspect ratio, and small H= values on a turbulent boundary-layer flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

wall-mounted cylinders with low AR, H=, and a low blockage ratio can be used to perturb the flow in the logarithmic and wake regions of a turbulent boundary layer by altering the organization of coherent vortical eddies.

the flowfield is significantly altered and modified by the presence of the cylinder(s), and that the flowfield downstream is characterized by a complex interaction between the cylinder(s) and the turbulent boundary layer.

the flow is modified in such a way as to produce a region with higher turbulence intensity and lower streamwise velocity, which is in agreement with the results of previous studies [14].

, while the cylinders do not appear to affect the mean flow significantly, the Reynolds stress and turbulent kinetic energy are affected.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the flowfield downstream of the wall-mounted cylinders is significantly altered by the presence of the cylinders, even when the cylinders have low blockage ratios and are arranged in sparse spanwise arrays.

the flow downstream of a single cylinder and a single row of cylinders is not significantly altered by the presence of the cylinder(s), and the cylinder array has a negligible effect on the boundary layer.
the organization of hairpin packets in the turbulent boundary layer is affected by wallmounted cylinder arrays.
